provenance.instrument: Warwick Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 195 Zoning, Ord. No. 2010-8 of 12-20-2010, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 WA1313, Township of Warwick, Bucks County (195-9 TOWNSHIP: 'Warwick Township, Bucks County, Pennsylvania'). Not Warwick Township, Lancaster County (Chapter 340, a separate code). Chapter 195 was adopted 12-20-2010 by Ord. No. 2010-8 and superseded the 1979 chapter. 195-16 was last amended 1-20-2025 by Ord. No. 2025-01, as were the R1, R1A, R2, C1, O and LI district articles. New Laws lists Ord. No. 2026-03 (7-23-2026, Zoning Amendment, Chapter 195) as not yet codified: its title adds data center rules and definitions and clarifies 'temporary sign', 'home occupation', 'buffer yard inclusions' and 'accessory structure placement'. Only the search excerpt was read. Ord. No. 2026-01 (certificates of use and occupancy) and 2026-04 (mass assemblies) are outside the zoning chapter
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 version information: 'Includes legislation through 11-17-2025' (search snippet). New Laws: Ord. No. 2026-03 (7-23-2026, Zoning Amendment) not yet in the text
provenance.code_caution: Ord. No. 2026-03 (adopted 7-23-2026) amends the zoning chapter, including 'accessory structure placement', and is not yet in the online text. Its text was not read. The accessory building placement rules here (195-16B(12)(b)) may have changed
checks: An accessory family apartment (Use B8) is a special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board in RA, R1, R1A, R2, RR and RG (195-16B(8)(f), 195-18C, 195-21C, 195-24C, 195-27C, 195-30C, 195-33C). The O District lists it among uses by right (195-53A), but 195-16B(8)(f) says 'This use may be permitted only by special exception'. It is not listed in MF-1, MF-2, C1, C2, C3, VC, VC 2 or LI, where an unlisted use is not permitted (195-11D)

Only relatives of the family living in the house may live in the unit (195-16B(8)(b)). The stated intent is family members related by blood or marriage to the owner of the house. The owner records a deed restriction in favor of the Township (195-16B(8)(i))
The unit is part of the house or in an accessory building that existed on April 1, 2011. No new separate building may be built for it, and it may not be in a cellar or basement (195-16B(8)(d))
At most 50% of the 'primary living area' of the house (living room, dining room, kitchen, one bathroom and the largest bedroom) and never more than 800 sq ft (195-16B(8)(a))

One unit per single-family detached dwelling, and no exterior change that suggests the house is other than a single-family detached dwelling (195-16B(8)(e)). Bucks County Board of Health approval of water and sewer (195-16B(8)(g))
Parking: two off-street spaces for the unit (195-16B(8)(h)), on top of the house's two (three with four or more bedrooms). Garage spaces do not count (195-16B(1)(a)[5])

Accessory buildings: at most 20 ft tall, at least 7 ft from any property line, and on lots under 3 acres in a side or rear yard no further forward than the front of the house; at most four accessory structures on lots under 3 acres (195-16B(12)(b)). Ord. No. 2026-03 (7-23-2026) 'clarifies accessory structure placement' and is not yet codified

Residential accessory uses by right (B12) include 'Living quarters for household employees, caretakers or watchmen, provided that no more than two such persons shall be provided with living quarters' (195-16B(12)(a)[4])
Two-family detached dwellings (duplex, one unit above the other) are permitted by right in MF-1, MF-2, C3 and O on 12,500 sq ft (40,000 sq ft without public sewer and water) (195-16B(1)(c))

In C1, C2, C3, VC and VC 2 an existing residential building may be converted into two or more units, or an accessory building into one or more units, by special exception (Use B7, 195-16B(7)): building at least seven years old, 1 acre lot, 12,000 sq ft per unit

A 'Dwelling in Combination' (Use G29) is 'An accessory dwelling unit that is clearly subordinate to an institutional, commercial, consumer service or office use': by right in VC and VC 2, special exception in C1, C2 and C3, at most 2 dwelling units per acre (195-16G(29))

On a farm, Use A2 Farm Unit allows detached dwelling units for the owner, the owner's parents, grandparents, siblings, sons and daughters and farm employees, at most 0.5 dwelling unit per acre (195-16A(2))
Three historic sites (195-144B) need a certificate of appropriateness for exterior changes (195-146, 195-148)
A garage or accessory building may be used as a dwelling only on a temporary zoning permit of up to one year (195-13A)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Warwick Township (Bucks County) Planning and Zoning. Read in a browser on eCode360, one page at a time, on 2026-11-15, mostly in print view. Searched the code (scope all, which also covers New Laws) for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, family apartment, ECHO, elder cottage, granny, relative, caretaker, guest house, carriage house, servants, tenant house, living quarters, immediate family, watchman, separate living, cooking facilities, tiny house, second dwelling, caregiver and sleeping quarters, then for two-family, double dwelling, conversion, manufactured, age-restricted, same general character, principal building, housekeeping, dwelling in combination, temporary dwelling and elderly, and New Laws (scope law). Read: 195-9 definitions, Article III (195-10 to 195-15 and 195-16A and B(1) to B(2) in full, B(7), B(8), B(12), G(29), I(3)), every district article IV to XVIII, Article XX (195-74 to 195-81), 195-117 and Article XXVII. Not read: 195-16B(3) to B(6), B(9) to B(11), the C to I uses beyond G29 and I3, Article XIX (natural resource protection and site capacity), Articles XXI, XXII, XXIV to XXVI and the Table of Use Regulations (Attachment 1, a PDF: the district sections give the same lists in text). No FAMILY definition was found. No bar on use variances (195-117)

term.value: accessory family apartment or dwelling unit
term.note: Use B8. The district lists call it 'Accessory Family Apartment'

status.note: Only relatives of the family in the house, by special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board

scope_districts.note: B8 is listed in RA, R1, R1A, R2, RR and RG as a special exception and in O among uses by right

status_outside.note: 'A use not listed in Articles IV through XVIII as noted above is not permitted in the specific zoning district.' B8 is not listed in MF-1, MF-2, C1, C2, C3, VC, VC 2 or LI

status_by_form.note: 'No new separate structures on the same lot with the principal residence shall be permitted to be constructed for this use'

path.note: 'This use may be permitted only by special exception to the Zoning Hearing Board.' The Board authorizes the zoning permit and may add restrictions (195-11B)

value.note: 195-53A (amended by Ord. No. 2018-1 and 2025-01) lists 'B8 Accessory Family Apartment' among 'Uses permitted by right', but 195-16B(8)(f) says the use 'may be permitted only by special exception to the Zoning Hearing Board'. Read as a special exception, the stricter of the two. Ask the zoning officer

fallback_path.note: Five findings of unnecessary hardship. No section read bars a use variance. A variance expires after one year unless construction starts (195-117C)

value.name: Dwelling in combination (Use G29), an accessory dwelling unit to a nonresidential use
value.conditions: 'An accessory dwelling unit that is clearly subordinate to an institutional, commercial, consumer service or office use' permitted in the district. The B8 floor area, lot area and parking rules apply (two spaces). At most 2.0 dwelling units per acre. Buffer yards (195-63). VC and VC 2 need public water and sewer
value.note: The host is a nonresidential use, not a house. VC and VC 2 permit no single-family detached dwelling

value.name: Dwelling in combination (Use G29), an accessory dwelling unit to a nonresidential use
value.conditions: 'An accessory dwelling unit that is clearly subordinate to an institutional, commercial, consumer service or office use' permitted in the district. The B8 floor area, lot area and parking rules apply (two spaces). At most 2.0 dwelling units per acre. Buffer yards (195-63)
value.note: The host is a nonresidential use, not a house. C1 and C2 permit no single-family detached dwelling, C3 none but twins and duplexes

value.name: Residential conversion (Use B7)
value.conditions: 'The conversion of an existing residential building in a commercial district into two or more dwelling units or the conversion of an accessory building into one or more dwelling units.' The building was built at least seven years before. 12,000 sq ft of lot per dwelling unit. Minimum floor area 400 sq ft for an efficiency, 500 for one bedroom, 650 for two. B1 lot width and yards. A single front entrance and no major exterior change. Separate cooking and sanitary facilities. Parking two spaces a unit (three with four or more bedrooms), beside or behind the building. 200 sq ft of recreation or patio area per unit

requires.condition: The building to be converted was constructed at least seven years before the conversion

value.note: 195-16B(7)(k) gives a 1 acre lot for C1, C2, O, VC and VC 2. C3 lists the use but is not in that table, and O is in the table but does not list the use. 12,000 sq ft per unit gives 24,000 sq ft for two units, under the 1 acre minimum

disputed_districts.note: C3 lists B7 by special exception, but the B7 lot area table names C1, C2, O, VC and VC 2 only, so the C3 lot minimum is not stated

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling (duplex, Use B1b)
value.conditions: 'A building on a single lot containing two dwelling units, each of which is totally separated from the other by an unpierced ceiling and floor extending from exterior wall to exterior wall, except for a common stairwell, exterior to both dwelling units.' Lot 12,500 sq ft, 60 ft wide, front 40 ft, side 15 ft, rear 30 ft, building coverage 35% (30% in C3), impervious 50% (40% in C3). A 50 ft perimeter buffer around a development of B1b uses. Parking two spaces a unit (three with four or more bedrooms)
value.note: A building type with one unit above the other. Whether an existing house may be altered into one is not stated

value.name: Living quarters for household employees, caretakers or watchmen (Use B12)
value.conditions: A residential accessory use: 'Living quarters for household employees, caretakers or watchmen, provided that no more than two such persons shall be provided with living quarters.' For employees of the household, not relatives. Accessory building rules apply (20 ft, 7 ft from property lines)
value.note: The code does not say whether the quarters may be a complete dwelling unit with a kitchen, or whether they may be in a new accessory building

value.name: Farm unit (Use A2)
value.conditions: 'Detached dwelling units for the sole use of the property owner, immediate family members of the property owner and persons engaged in agricultural employment on the property. Immediate family members shall be limited to parents, grandparents, siblings, sons and daughters.' An accessory use to a farm use (A1, A4, A6, A7, A8 or A9), at most 0.5 dwelling unit per acre, B1 yards from lot lines and between farm units, two parking spaces a unit. General farming (A1) needs 2 acres

requires.condition: The lot is in a principal farm use (A1 General Farming, A4, A6, A7, A8 or A9)

value.note: At 0.5 dwelling unit per acre a house and one farm unit would need 4 acres, if the house counts toward the density. The code does not say

building_types.note: 'One apartment or dwelling unit accessory to a single-family detached dwelling'

historic_bypass.note: No historic ADU path found. Historic sites take the uses of their district (195-147)

districts_read_no_listing.note: B8 is not listed. MF-1 and MF-2 permit single-family detached dwellings, twins and duplexes. C3 permits twins and duplexes. C1, C2, VC, VC 2 and LI permit no single-family dwelling

value.condition: Only relatives of the family living in the house may occupy the unit. The intent is family members related by blood or marriage to the owner of the house, and the code bars for-profit apartments.
A unit outside the house is allowed only in an accessory structure or building that existed on April 1, 2011. No new separate structure may be built for it.

The unit may not be in a cellar or basement (a space with half or more of its height below the adjoining ground). One unit per house, and no exterior change that suggests the house is other than a single-family detached dwelling.
The owner shows the Township approval by the Bucks County Board of Health of the water and sewer facilities serving the site.
The record owner grants the Township a deed restriction limiting the use to these provisions, at the owner's cost.

On the three designated historic sites (Neshaminy-Warwick Presbyterian Church and its graveyard, Moland House) exterior changes need a certificate of appropriateness from the Board of Supervisors on the advice of the Board of Historical Architectural Review.

types_allowed.note: 'Such use may be part of the principal residence or may be contained in an accessory structure or building existing as of April 1, 2011.' A unit in a garage or above it counts only in a building that existed on that date

types_not_addressed.note: An addition becomes 'part of the principal residence', but 195-16B(8)(e) bars exterior changes that suggest the house is other than a single-family detached dwelling. The code does not say whether an addition for the unit is allowed

value.garage_conversion: In an accessory building that existed on April 1, 2011
value.over_garage: Upstairs in an accessory building that existed on April 1, 2011

max_sqft.note: 'in no event shall the accessory use exceed a total floor area of 800 square feet'

value.part: the primary living area of the house (living room, dining room, kitchen, one bathroom and the largest bedroom)

max_share_of_part.note: 'Such use shall occupy no more than 50% of the total floor area of the primary living area of the principal residence ... The primary living area includes a living room, dining room, kitchen, one bathroom and the largest bedroom.'

max_height_ft.note: 'All accessory buildings or uses shall not exceed 20 feet in height'. The unit is in an existing accessory building, so it is already within the building's height

internal_uses_district_height.note: 35 ft in every district that lists B8

setback_side_ft.note: 'on properties of any size ... the accessory building shall be located no less than seven feet from any property line'

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: 195-78 says no building may be built within the minimum front, side or rear yards, but 195-16B(12)(b)[1] places accessory buildings in side and rear yards 7 ft from property lines. Read with the specific accessory rule. An existing accessory building keeps its place

accessory_cap_binds_adu.note: The 20 ft limit reaches 'All accessory buildings or uses'

value.where: On a lot under 3 acres: only in a side or rear yard, no further forward than the front of the house (a corner lot may pick one front yard not facing the street the house faces). At most four accessory structures (sheds, garages, pool houses, barns and the like) on the lot
value.note: Ord. No. 2026-03 (7-23-2026, not yet codified) clarifies accessory structure placement

occupancy.value: Relatives of the family living in the house. The intent names family members related by blood or marriage to the owner of the house. No for-profit apartment.
occupancy.note: 'B8 Accessory Family Apartment or Dwelling Unit. One apartment or dwelling unit accessory to a single-family detached dwelling shall be permitted provided the following conditions are met. The intent of these provisions is to allow for family members related by blood or marriage to the owner of the principal residence to reside on the premises, but to prohibit the creation of for-profit apartments in districts where multifamily housing is not otherwise permitted.' (b): 'Occupancy of such use shall include only relatives of the family occupying the principal residence.'

owner_occupancy.note: No owner-occupancy rule. The intent speaks of relatives of 'the owner of the principal residence', and (b) of relatives of 'the family occupying the principal residence'

max_adus.note: 'Only one accessory family apartment shall be permitted per single-family detached dwelling'

spaces_required.note: 'two off-street parking spaces shall be provided for the additional use'

reading.value: Two spaces for the unit plus the house's own: two for a house with three bedrooms or fewer, three with four or more. Spaces inside a garage do not count. So four or five off-street spaces in all.
